depiction.composition: centered checkmark enclosed in a plain ring

ambiguity: In a to-do app, a circled checkmark looks identical to the task-completion checkbox itself, making an uncompleted task look already finished.
task_intents: set up personal task manager workflow

example_tasks.task: Give final approval on the contractor's revised kitchen cabinet quote
Confirm headcount with the catering company by Wednesday noon
Complete identity verification step for the new brokerage account
Sign off on the release candidate after staging tests pass
Clean up stale items in my weekly GTD review list
Go through the pending expense approvals in Concur before payroll closes on Friday
Confirm with all three references that they are okay being contacted this week
Run through the pre-trip campervan readiness checklist before leaving the driveway on Saturday

context_tasks.task: Inspect fire extinguishers on the second floor
Vote in the local school board election

near_misses.task: Check tyre pressure before the road trip
Write a check for the plumber
Check in for the 6am flight to Madrid
Verify that the backup drive is still mounted
Buy a checked shirt for the autumn party

reasoning: A checkmark inside a circle is the universal UI control for a completed task in a to-do list, so displaying it as a task's subject icon visually collides with the completion checkbox. Furthermore, it represents a status ('done') or generic verb ('check', 'verify', 'approve') rather than a concrete subject.
